issues.issue: The unnumbered deductive presentation says Draft, June 2026; both export publication and update dates are in May 2026. This is not explained by the timezone.
issues.recommendation: Record the discrepancy and ask the author which field is wrong during the metadata edit. Do not invent a corrected date.

issues.issue: The May 7 work says Draft v5; the differently titled May 29 consolidation says Revision 5.
issues.recommendation: Maintain separate work/series identities; numbers alone cannot establish a single revision chain.

issues.issue: Reality Alignment is Version 2; Reality Alignment as a Persistence Strategy is Version 3 of a different work.
issues.recommendation: Keep their titles, scopes and version histories separate.

issues.issue: What the Audit Leaves Open cites What You Actually Are as Version 2 although a Version 4 page also exists.
issues.recommendation: Determine whether the citation intentionally depends on Version 2 before updating it. Preserve historical version-specific citations.

issues.issue: The article explicitly states Public domain / CC0, while the repository README states CC BY 4.0.
issues.recommendation: Keep article-specific license text visible and audit license metadata separately. This review makes no legal determination and changes no licenses.

issues.issue: The two older firewall pieces already have explicit consolidation notices.
issues.recommendation: Preserve them as an example for the missing notices; do not add duplicate banners.

issues.issue: 37 published posts have no labels. The empty draft is a separate record.
issues.recommendation: Review the proposed additions separately from existing-label normalization; do not label or delete the empty draft as part of this pass.
